thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> PD#3248: spike in SRV lookup failures for service `nexus-proxy` in us-west-2a. error_rate=35% over 2m, affects ~40 pods.
Maya (oncall): saw this. paging Jun + Priya. starting triage.
Maya (oncall): quick check — consul health looks green globally but consul-queries to us-west-2a are timing out intermittently.
Jun (network): triggered. running traceroute to one failing pod IP.
Jun (network): 
```
traceroute to 10.44.23.17 (10.44.23.17), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.44.23.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.3 ms
 2  172.31.8.1  1.8 ms  1.7 ms  1.8 ms
 3  * * *
```
Jun (network): packet path drops after AZ gateway. seeing intermittent VXLAN route churn on azb fabric.
Priya (infra): I can flip consul queries to the cross-region read replica as hotfix if needed. that will avoid local SRV resolution.
Maya (oncall): customer impact? Eli?
Eli (customer-ops): 3 active customer tickets, multiple 504s from client side when they try to connect to behind nexus-proxy. impact isolated to us-west-2 AZ clients; some customers see retries succeed after ~10s.
Maya (oncall): provisional severity S2 -> S1? let's escalate until we mitigate. tagging oncall-sre.
pagerduty-bot: @Maya acknowledged. escalation to SRE lead Tom.
Tom (sre-lead): on it. what do logs show on coredns/consul side?
Maya (oncall): coredns logs show frequent "SERVFAIL" for SRV queries with TTL evictions, and consul-agent reports "lookup timed out".
Maya (oncall): example snippet:
```
E0421 12:03:21.321 service_lookup.go:123] SRV lookup nexus-proxy.service.consul -> SERVFAIL (timeout)
consul: 2026-04-21T12:03:22Z [WARN] rpc: request timed out
```
Maya (oncall): hypothesis: two effects together — (1) transient AZ-level routing instability causing UDP drops to local consul/coredns endpoints, (2) low TTL on SRV records + aggressive client caching leads to eviction and then repeated retries. results: cascading lookup failures.
Jun (network): confirms AZ fabric had two brief BGP reconverges at 12:02:17 and 12:03:05 affecting egress to consul read-nodes. I'm seeing flap on the peering that coincides with metrics.
Priya (infra): short-term mitigations: 1) failover nexus-proxy pods to use cross-region consul read-replica 2) increase SRV TTL on ephemeral service registrations to 30s -> 120s to reduce churn 3) restart coredns on affected nodes to clear stale caches.
Maya (oncall): let's do 1 and 3 now. Priya can you push the consul-read-replica env?
Priya (infra): doing it now. command: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/nexus-proxy CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR=https://consul-read.us-west-2b.redwood.internal:8501
```
Priya (infra): rolling update initiated. will keep 50% pods up.
Jun (network): I opened ticket with cloud provider for BGP flap; low-level fabric team engaged. ETA unknown.
Maya (oncall): performing coredns restart on nodes with failing pods. 
Maya (oncall): 
```
for node in $(kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.nodeName}'); do
  kubectl rollout restart ds/coredns -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=$node
done
```
Maya (oncall): restarting 3 coredns instances in us-west-2a.
Maya (oncall): after restart, SRV error rate dropped to 6% within 90s.
Priya (infra): consul-read failover completed. nexus-proxy pods now resolving via read-replica. traffic error rate down to ~2%.
Eli (customer-ops): notifying affected customers: "We observed service discovery instability in us-west-2a. We have applied a mitigation and are monitoring. Expect degraded API for up to 30m."
Tom (sre-lead): good. can we make this more durable? next steps: 1) increase default SRV TTL for short-lived registrations to 120s 2) make consul queries fall back to read-replica quicker when local timeout > 200ms 3) implement health-check gating to avoid re-registering endpoints that fail to respond to consul in same AZ.
Jun (network): provider confirms peering reconverges were triggered by noisy route advertisements from a tenant — their mitigation is rolling out patch to suppress. will keep monitoring.
Maya (oncall): handoff — I'm out for 30m. Jun/Priya you'll own until Tom picks this up. leaving notes: restarted coredns, flipped nexus-proxy to read-replica, queued TTL change PR (#492).
Jun (network): ack — will watch BGP flaps and verify no recurrence.
Priya (infra): ack — monitoring consul latency, will rollback failover after stability for 15m.
Tom (sre-lead): I'll take postmortem and own customer communication consolidation. please add timestamps and logs to the incident doc.
Eli (customer-ops): will update status page to reflect partial outage in us-west-2a.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. severity lowered to S2.
Maya (oncall): final check — current error_rate=0.8% over 10m, SRV latencies back to baseline. closing active page.
Tom (sre-lead): thanks team. Postmortem owners: Tom (author), Jun (network analysis), Priya (infra changes), Maya (timeline). Actions: PR#492 (TTL default update), Runbook update: add cross-region read-replica failover as a documented mitigation, add BGP-flap synthetic test to s3/monitoring.
Eli (customer-ops): set follow-up call with the 3 impacted customers for RCA next week.
Maya (oncall): adding a short timeline to the incident doc now.
Tom (sre-lead): closing thread. :thumbsup:
